X.label: X axis, a diameter on a lathe
X.description: On a lathe, the position across the turning axis; it is a diameter while diameter programming is on, which is how the turning profile starts. On a milling machine it is an ordinary position, and the milling profile starts with diameter programming off.

Z.label: Z axis
Z.description: Position along the turning axis on a lathe, and along the tool axis on a milling machine working in G17.

C.label: C axis
C.description: An angle: on a lathe the angle of the spindle, used to place holes and flats for driven tools; on a milling machine usually a rotary table or head.

Y.label: Y axis
Y.description: Position on Y: across the turning axis on a lathe that has a Y axis, the second axis of the working plane on a milling machine.

I.label: Arc centre on X, or a thread lead
I.description: Distance from the start point to the arc centre across the turning axis. In a thread block it is the lead instead, for G34 and G35 the lead at the start of the thread.

J.label: Arc centre on Y, or a thread lead
J.description: Distance from the start point to the arc centre along Y. In a thread block it is the lead instead, for G34 and G35 the lead at the start of the thread.

K.label: Arc centre on Z, or a thread lead
K.description: Distance from the start point to the arc centre along the turning axis. In a thread block it is the lead instead, for G34 and G35 the lead at the start of the thread.

CR.label: Arc radius
CR.description: Radius of an arc, written instead of the centre. A negative radius picks the arc longer than half a circle. It is always written with an equals sign.

AR.label: Opening angle
AR.description: Angle an arc sweeps, written instead of the end point or the centre. It is always written with an equals sign.

LIMS.label: Spindle speed limit
LIMS.description: Highest speed the control may run under G96, G961 and G97 (not under G971). It is a limit, not a speed: changing it changes the guard the programmer set. It cannot raise the G26 or setting-data limit, stays in force after the program ends, and LIMS[n]= sets it for spindle n.

SF.label: Thread start angle
SF.description: Angle at which a thread starts, used for multi-start threads.

D.label: Cutting edge
D.description: Offset set of the active tool. D0 switches the length and radius offsets off.

F.label: Feed, or dwell time
F.description: Feed rate. Its unit follows the feed type in force: a distance per minute with G94, G961 and G971, per spindle revolution with G95, G96, G97 and G973. With G4 it is a dwell in seconds, and with G34 or G35 the change of the thread lead per revolution.

S.label: Spindle speed
S.description: Spindle speed in revolutions per minute, or the cutting speed while G96, G961 or G962 is active. With G4 it is a dwell in spindle revolutions, and with G25 or G26 a speed limit. A number in the address, as in S3=, names the spindle it is for; a plain S is meant for the master spindle, which SETMS can change.

T.label: Tool
T.description: Tool number, or the tool name in quotation marks where the machine manages tools by name. T0 deselects the tool.

N.label: Block number
N.description: Number of the block. It is optional, and the control does not require the numbers to be in order.

L.label: Subprogram call
L.description: Calls the subprogram of that number. The digits are the program's name, leading zeros included, so L12 and L012 call two different programs.

P.label: Repeat count
P.description: How often the subprogram called in the same block runs.

G.label: Preparatory function
G.description: Selects how the control reads the rest of the block: the kind of movement, the plane, the feed mode and the measuring modes.

M.label: Machine function
M.description: Switches a machine function such as the spindle, the coolant or the program end. Numbers above 30 are set up by the machine builder and are not errors.

codes.label: Rapid
codes.description: Moves to the position at rapid speed.

codes.label: Linear feed move
codes.description: Moves to the position on a straight line at the feed in F.

codes.label: Arc, clockwise
codes.description: Cuts an arc clockwise to the end point in the axis words. I, J and K give the centre.

codes.label: Arc, counter-clockwise
codes.description: Cuts an arc counter-clockwise, described the same way as G2.

codes.label: Arc through a point
codes.description: Cuts an arc through an intermediate point given with I1=, J1= and K1=.

codes.label: Arc, tangential
codes.description: Cuts an arc that joins the path before it without a corner. Only the end point is given.

codes.label: Dwell
codes.description: Holds the position for the time in F, in seconds, or for the number of spindle revolutions in S; S2= and the like count the revolutions of another spindle. It stands in a block of its own. That F is not a feed and that S is not a speed, so nothing that scales feeds or speeds may touch them.

codes.label: Tapping with a compensating chuck, one block
codes.description: Taps to the position in the block with the spindle not under position control; the chuck takes up the difference. F has to be the spindle speed times the thread pitch, so the two may only be changed together. The move type in force before it applies again in the next block.

codes.label: Exact stop, this block only
codes.description: Brings the axes to a stop inside the position window at the end of this block, without changing the path mode that follows.

codes.label: Exact stop mode
codes.description: Stops at the end of every block until another path mode replaces it, so each corner is cut sharp.

codes.label: Continuous path mode
codes.description: Keeps the axes moving from one block into the next instead of stopping at every block end; the control slows down at a corner as far as it has to.

codes.label: Continuous path, rounded by distance
codes.description: Rounds a corner within the distance given by ADIS.

codes.label: Continuous path, rounded by axis tolerance
codes.description: Rounds a corner within the tolerance each axis is allowed. Programs written by CAM often carry it.

codes.label: Continuous path, rounded on tangential corners too
Working plane ZX
codes.description: The plane a turning program works in.

codes.label: Thread cutting
codes.description: Cuts a thread with a constant lead, given in I, J or K. The lead is not a feed and may never be scaled like one.

codes.label: Rigid tapping, into the hole
codes.description: Drives the tap with the spindle under position control; the lead is in I, J or K and is not a feed. S is read in revolutions per minute here, whatever the feed type says.

codes.label: Rigid tapping, back out
codes.description: The retract of a rigid tapping pass, with the same lead as the block that cut it.

codes.label: Thread cutting, lead growing
codes.description: Cuts a thread whose lead grows along the thread: I, J or K give the lead at the start, and F the change of the lead per revolution. Neither is a feed, and nothing may scale them.

params.label: Lead along X at the start
Lead along Y at the start
Lead along Z at the start
Change of the lead per revolution

codes.label: Thread cutting, lead shrinking
codes.description: Cuts a thread whose lead shrinks along the thread: I, J or K give the lead at the start, and F the change of the lead per revolution. Neither is a feed, and nothing may scale them.

params.label: Lead along X at the start
Lead along Y at the start
Lead along Z at the start
Change of the lead per revolution

codes.label: Thread along an arc, clockwise
codes.description: Cuts a thread whose path is a clockwise arc instead of a straight line. The lead is in I, J or K as with G33, so the arc centre is written as IR=, JR= and KR=.

codes.label: Thread along an arc, counter-clockwise
codes.description: Cuts a thread whose path is a counter-clockwise arc instead of a straight line. The lead is in I, J or K as with G33, so the arc centre is written as IR=, JR= and KR=.

codes.label: Radius compensation, tool left
codes.description: Offsets the path by the radius of the edge that D selects, seen along the direction of travel.

codes.label: Suppress the offsets for this block
codes.description: Runs this block without the work offsets.

codes.label: Suppress the offsets for this block, more of them than G53
codes.description: Leaves out more of the offsets than G53 does, for this block only. Programs use it to move to a machine position, as before a tool change.

codes.label: Reference point approach
codes.description: Moves the machine axes written with it, as X1=0 Z1=0, to their reference points. The values say which axes move, not where to. It stands in a block of its own, and no transformation may be on for those axes.

codes.label: Approach a fixed machine point
codes.description: Moves the axes written with it, each on its own and at rapid traverse, to the fixed point FP= names (1 to 4; none or 0 is 1), a position set in machine data and reached in machine coordinates. The values of the axis words are not positions, which is why posts write 0. Milling posts use it to retract before a tool change; it is not allowed while radius compensation or a transformation is on.

codes.label: Settable work offset off
codes.description: Cancels the settable work offset. Programs often write it in the header.

codes.label: Inch for the geometry
codes.description: Reads the positions as inches. It is a unit switch on this control and not a finishing cycle.

codes.label: Millimetres for the geometry
codes.description: Reads the positions as millimetres. It is a unit switch on this control and not a roughing cycle.

codes.label: Inch for the geometry and the feed
Millimetres for the geometry and the feed
Absolute positions
codes.description: Reads every position as a distance from the zero point.

codes.label: Incremental positions
codes.description: Reads every position as a distance from the point before.

codes.label: Inverse-time feed
codes.description: F is the reciprocal of the time the block takes, not a distance. It also ends a constant cutting speed, so S is in revolutions per minute.

codes.label: Feed per minute
codes.description: F is a distance per minute from here on, and S a speed in revolutions per minute: it also ends a constant cutting speed.

codes.label: Feed per revolution
codes.description: F is a distance per spindle revolution from here on, which is how turning programs cut, and S a speed in revolutions per minute: it also ends a constant cutting speed.

codes.label: Constant cutting speed, feed per revolution
codes.description: S is a cutting speed from here on, and the control changes the spindle speed with the diameter. It also makes F a distance per revolution. A speed limit belongs with it, written as LIMS=.

codes.label: Fixed spindle speed, feed per revolution
codes.description: S is a speed in revolutions per minute again, and F a distance per revolution. Without a new S the spindle keeps the speed it was turning at.

codes.label: Feed given by travel time
codes.description: F is the time the block's move takes, not a distance per minute: a larger F is a slower move. It also ends a constant cutting speed, so S is in revolutions per minute.

codes.label: Constant cutting speed, feed per minute
codes.description: As G96, but F is a distance per minute.

codes.label: Constant cutting speed, feed type kept
codes.description: As G96, but F keeps the unit it had: per minute or per revolution.

codes.label: Fixed spindle speed, feed per minute
codes.description: As G97, but F is a distance per minute. A LIMS= limit does not act under it.

codes.label: Fixed spindle speed, feed type kept
codes.description: As G97, but F keeps the unit it had: per minute or per revolution.

codes.label: Fixed spindle speed without a speed limit
codes.description: As G97, but no LIMS= limit is switched on with it.

codes.label: Feed per minute, spindle speed frozen
codes.description: F is a distance per minute, and the spindle keeps the speed it is turning at, whether a cutting speed or an S set it.

codes.label: Feed per revolution, spindle speed frozen
codes.description: F is a distance per revolution, and the spindle keeps the speed it is turning at, whether a cutting speed or an S set it.

codes.label: Lower limit: spindle speed with S, working area with axis words
codes.description: With S the lowest speed the master spindle may run at, and S2=, S3= set it for the spindle of that number; with axis words the lower end of the working area. Either way it is a limit, not a speed or a position to move to. The control stores it in its settings, so it can still be in force after the program ends.

codes.label: Upper limit: spindle speed with S, working area with axis words
codes.description: With S the highest speed the master spindle may run at, and S2=, S3= set it for the spindle of that number; with axis words the upper end of the working area. Either way it is a limit, not a speed or a position to move to. The control stores it in its settings, so it can still be in force after the program ends.

codes.label: Diameter programming on
codes.description: Reads the cross axis as a diameter from here on. gEdit also assumes it at the start of a program, unless the machine configuration says the control starts without it.

codes.label: Diameter programming off
codes.description: Reads the cross axis as a radius from here on.

codes.label: Diameter for absolute values only
codes.description: Reads absolute positions on the cross axis as diameters and incremental ones as radii.

codes.label: Drilling or centring cycle
codes.description: Drills to depth in one pass and retracts. The plane, the depth and the safety distance come in the order below.

codes.label: Drilling cycle with a dwell
codes.description: Drills to depth, waits there and retracts, which is what a counterbore needs.

codes.description: Drills in pecks, so the chips break or leave the hole. VARI decides between breaking the chip and pulling the drill out.

codes.label: Rigid tapping cycle
codes.description: Cuts the thread with the spindle under position control, so no compensating chuck is needed. The lead (MPIT or PIT) and the tapping speed (SST) are its own arguments: it does not take its lead from the feed in force.

codes.label: Reaming cycle, feed in and feed out
codes.description: Feeds in and feeds back out, so the bore keeps its finish. The two feeds are given separately.

codes.label: Boring cycle with an oriented stop
codes.description: Stops the spindle at an angle at depth, lifts the tool off the wall and pulls it out at rapid.

codes.label: Boring cycle with a stop at depth
codes.description: Bores to depth, then stops the spindle without orienting it and stops the program. On the next NC start the cycle pulls the tool out to the retraction plane at rapid by itself.

codes.label: Boring cycle with a dwell and a stop at depth
codes.description: Like CYCLE87 with a dwell at depth: waits, stops the spindle and the program, and pulls out at rapid on the next NC start.

codes.description: Waits at depth and feeds back out at the cutting feed, then leaves at rapid.

codes.label: Grooving cycle
codes.description: Cuts a groove on the outside, the inside or the face. The name is recognised; the parameters are not described yet.

codes.label: Stock removal cycle
codes.description: Roughs and finishes along a contour that a subprogram describes. Its three feeds, for roughing, for plunging into undercuts and for finishing, are arguments.

params.label: Largest depth of cut when roughing
Kind of machining: roughing, finishing or both, along or across, outside or inside
Whether the depth of cut follows the diameter mode

codes.label: Thread cutting cycle
codes.description: Cuts a thread in several passes. The lead is one of its arguments, not the feed in force. The parameters are not described yet.

codes.label: Thread turning cycle
codes.description: Cuts a thread in several passes, along Z, across X or on a taper. The pitch is its own argument (PIT), not the feed in force.

params.label: Reference point in X, as a diameter
Infeed slope, as a distance or an angle

codes.label: Parting-off cycle
codes.description: Parts the workpiece off and lowers speed and feed for the last part of the cut. Its speeds and feeds are arguments.

codes.description: Cuts one groove or a row of grooves, with slopes, radii or chamfers at its edges. Its feed is argument 21.

codes.label: Undercut cycle
codes.description: Cuts a relief groove of form E or F, or an undercut for a thread. The parameters are not described yet.

codes.label: Stock removal cycle for a corner
codes.description: Removes stock at a corner given by points in its arguments, with radii or chamfers. Its feed is argument 16.

Intermediate point in X, or an angle
Intermediate point in Z, or an angle
Where the corner lies: outside or inside, back or front

codes.label: Contour turning and grooving cycle
codes.description: Turns, grooves or plunge-turns along a contour, rest material included. Its feeds are arguments 5 and 6 (one per axis when it plunge-turns), and 34 for the finishing cut when one call roughs and finishes.

codes.label: Thread chain cycle
codes.description: Cuts several thread sections one after the other. The lead is one of its arguments. The parameters are not described yet.

codes.label: Contour call
codes.description: Names the contour the turning cycle after it works on. It cuts nothing itself.

codes.label: Swivel the working plane
codes.description: Swivels the working plane for 3+2 machining, or swivels or aligns the tool, with the swivel data set named in the second argument, and sets the frame that goes with it. Written with no arguments, CYCLE800() clears the swivel and its frames, which is why posts write it at the start of a program, some without the brackets. The reference points before and after the rotation are absolute positions. Older control versions take 15 arguments, without the last one.

Swivel mode, bit-coded: how the three angles are read (axis by axis, solid angle, projection angle, rotary axes directly) and the order of the rotations

codes.label: High-speed settings
codes.description: Sets the contour tolerance and the machining type for the following moves, and with them the path mode, the compressor, smoothing and feed-forward, so a program that calls it does not write those itself. CYCLE832() or a tolerance of 0 switches it off. The second argument is a number or a word: _FINISH, _SEMIFIN, _ROUGH, _PRECISION, the same with _ORI_ in front when the third argument is an orientation tolerance, and _OFF. Older control versions read the second argument as a packed code of several digits, so its value is shown as written and not decoded.

params.label: Contour tolerance of the geometry axes; 0 switches the settings off
Machining type: 0 off, 1 finish, 2 semi-finish, 3 rough, 4 precision; plus 10 when S_OTOL is an orientation tolerance
Orientation tolerance, or a version mark; it is written on a three-axis machine too

codes.label: Program stop
codes.description: Stops the program until the operator starts it again.

codes.label: Optional stop
codes.description: Stops the program when the operator has switched optional stop on.

codes.label: End of subprogram
codes.description: Ends a subprogram and goes on after the block that called it.

codes.label: Spindle on, clockwise
codes.description: Starts the master spindle clockwise. M3=3 does the same for spindle 3.

codes.label: Spindle on, counter-clockwise
codes.description: Starts the master spindle counter-clockwise. M3=4 does the same for spindle 3.

codes.label: Spindle stop
codes.description: Stops the master spindle. M3=5 stops spindle 3.

codes.label: Tool change
codes.description: Changes the tool: loads the tool selected with T. A milling machine changes its tools this way; whether a turret changes on the T word alone or needs this code is set up on the machine.

codes.label: Spindle orientation
codes.description: Turns the spindle to the angle kept in the control's setting data and holds it there until the next M3, M4 or M5. M2=19 does the same for spindle 2.

codes.label: Automatic gear stage
codes.description: Lets the control choose the gear stage from the programmed speed.

codes.label: Spindle to axis mode
codes.description: Switches the spindle over to position control as a rotary axis.

codes.label: Cutting speed of the tool
codes.description: SVC=100 gives the cutting speed of the active milling or drilling tool in metres per minute, feet in an inch program; the control works out the spindle speed from the tool radius. Without an index it is meant for the master spindle, SVC[2]= for spindle 2. An S word ends it, and so do G96 and SPOS.

codes.label: Choose the master spindle
codes.description: SETMS(3) makes spindle 3 the master spindle, so the S, M3, M4 and M5 that follow without a spindle number are meant for it. SETMS on its own goes back to the master spindle the machine is set up with. It stands in a block of its own.

codes.label: Operator message
codes.description: Shows the text in the brackets on the control. MSG() with nothing inside clears it.

codes.label: Modal cycle call
codes.description: Makes the cycle or subprogram written after it run after every following block that moves, until MCALL stands on its own.

codes.label: Stop the look-ahead
codes.description: Makes the control finish the blocks it has already read before it goes on.

codes.label: Suppress the offsets for this block, all of them
codes.description: The widest of G53, G153 and SUPA: this block runs in machine coordinates.

codes.label: Face transformation on
codes.description: Turns on the transformation that lets a driven tool work on the face with X and Y.

codes.label: Cylinder surface transformation on
codes.description: Turns on the transformation for work on the cylinder surface, where one axis word is a distance along the unrolled surface. TRAFOOF ends it.

codes.label: Transformation off
codes.description: Ends the transformation that is running: TRAORI, TRANSMIT, TRACYL or TRAANG. G74 and G75 do not run while one is on.

codes.label: Five-axis transformation on
codes.description: Turns on the orientation transformation of a four- or five-axis machine: from here on X, Y and Z are the position of the tool tip and the rotary axis words or the orientation words set the tool direction, while the control moves the machine axes to suit. TRAORI(n) picks the transformation set up as number n; further arguments give the basic tool orientation and offsets of the rotary axes. TRAFOOF ends it.

codes.label: Programmable offset
codes.description: Shifts the zero point by the values in the block. Written on its own it clears the programmable frame.

codes.label: Additive programmable offset
codes.description: Shifts the zero point by the values in the block, on top of the frame already programmed.

codes.label: Programmable rotation
codes.description: Turns the coordinate system by the angles written for the axes, or by RPL= about the axis normal to the working plane, and replaces every frame instruction programmed before it. The axis words are angles, not positions. Written on its own it clears the programmable frame.

codes.label: Additive programmable rotation
codes.description: Turns the coordinate system by the angles written for the axes, or by RPL=, on top of the frame already programmed. The axis words are angles, not positions.

codes.label: Compressor on
codes.description: Joins short straight blocks into a smoother path.

codes.label: Approach and leave the contour straight
codes.description: With G41 or G42 (approach) and G40 (retract): the tool moves to the contour point on a straight line and stands square to the contour there.

codes.label: Approach and leave around the contour point
codes.description: With G41 or G42 and G40: the tool goes around the start or end point of the contour the way G450 or G451 sets for corners.

codes.label: Approach and leave with continuous curvature
codes.description: With G41 or G42 and G40: the control replaces the approach and retract G1 blocks by a curve whose direction and curvature meet the contour without a jump.

codes.label: Approach and leave with continuous tangent
codes.description: With G41 or G42 and G40: the control replaces the approach and retract G1 blocks by a curve whose direction meets the contour without a jump.

codes.label: Single block off
codes.description: In single-block mode the control no longer stops after each block: the blocks up to SBLON (or the end of the subprogram) run like one block. It stands in a PROC line or alone in its block.

codes.label: Single block on
codes.description: Ends what SBLOF started: in single-block mode the control stops after each block again. It stands alone in its block.

codes.label: Hide the current block
codes.description: Written at the end of a PROC line: while this subprogram runs, the block display shows its call instead of its blocks, up to the return.

codes.label: Show the current block
codes.description: Written at the end of a PROC line: this subprogram shows its own blocks again, even when it is called from one that hides them.

codes.label: Orientation in workpiece coordinates
codes.description: The tool direction a five-axis program writes is read in workpiece coordinates, so it does not depend on the machine the program runs on. It is the control's basic setting.

codes.label: Orientation in machine coordinates
codes.description: The tool direction a five-axis program writes is read in machine coordinates, so the rotary axes move as the machine is built.

codes.label: Interpolate the orientation axis by axis
codes.description: Changes the tool direction by moving each rotary axis in a straight line from its start to its end value.

codes.label: Interpolate the orientation as a vector
codes.description: Changes the tool direction along a great circle, in the plane the start and end direction span. ORIPLANE does the same.

codes.label: Interpolate the orientation in a plane
codes.description: Changes the tool direction along a great circle, in the plane the start and end direction span, as ORIVECT does.

codes.label: Tool orientation relative to the path
codes.description: The tool direction is given relative to the path and the surface, by the lead angle LEAD= and the tilt angle TILT=.

codes.label: Orientation angles read as Euler angles
codes.description: A2=, B2= and C2= are read as Euler angles, in degrees, turned in the order Z, X', Z''.

codes.label: Orientation angles read as RPY angles, X Y Z
codes.description: A2=, B2= and C2= are read as roll, pitch and yaw angles, in degrees, turned about X, then Y, then Z.

codes.label: Orientation angles read as RPY angles, Z Y X
codes.description: A2=, B2= and C2= are read as roll, pitch and yaw angles, in degrees, turned about Z, then Y, then X.

codes.label: Orientation angles of virtual axes, first definition
codes.description: A2=, B2= and C2= are the angles of virtual orientation axes, turned in the order machine data sets up as the first definition.

codes.label: Orientation angles of virtual axes, second definition
codes.description: A2=, B2= and C2= are the angles of virtual orientation axes, turned in the order machine data sets up as the second definition.

codes.label: Move the orientation axes to their basic position
codes.description: Moves the rotary axes of the orientation together, in straight lines, to the positions written in brackets; an axis with no value goes to the basic position set in machine data. Active frames of the rotary axes are not taken into account. Only while TRAORI is on.

codes.label: Dynamics for normal travel
codes.description: Switches the path to the acceleration and jerk values the machine builder set up for normal travel. The values are machine data. It acts from the block it stands in, without a stop.

codes.label: Dynamics for positioning and tapping
codes.description: Switches the path to the acceleration and jerk values the machine builder set up for positioning and tapping. The values are machine data. It acts from the block it stands in, without a stop.

codes.label: Dynamics for roughing
codes.description: Switches the path to the acceleration and jerk values the machine builder set up for roughing. The values are machine data. It acts from the block it stands in, without a stop.

codes.label: Dynamics for semi-finishing
codes.description: Switches the path to the acceleration and jerk values the machine builder set up for semi-finishing. The values are machine data. It acts from the block it stands in, without a stop.

codes.label: Dynamics for finishing
codes.description: Switches the path to the acceleration and jerk values the machine builder set up for finishing. The values are machine data. It acts from the block it stands in, without a stop.

codes.label: Dynamics for precision finishing
codes.description: Switches the path to the acceleration and jerk values the machine builder set up for precision finishing. The values are machine data. It acts from the block it stands in, without a stop.

codes.label: This value is absolute
codes.description: Reads the one value in brackets as an absolute position, whatever the distance mode says.

codes.label: Jump forward
codes.description: Continues at the label, searching towards the end of the program.

codes.label: Jump backward
codes.description: Continues at the label, searching towards the start of the program.

codes.label: Jump
codes.description: Continues at the label or the block number, searching forwards first and then backwards.

codes.label: Jump without an alarm
codes.description: Like GOTO, but the control does not stop when the target is missing.

codes.label: Conditional
codes.description: Runs what follows when the condition holds.

codes.label: Upper bound of a counting loop
Repeat loop, or a section between two labels
Branch of CASE for every other value
Return from a subprogram
codes.description: Returns from a subprogram to the block after the call, as M17 does. It stands in a block of its own.

codes.label: Subprogram head
codes.description: Names a subprogram and the values it takes. It is the first statement of the program.

codes.label: Declare a subprogram
codes.description: Tells the calling program the name and the values of a subprogram that is not in the cycle folders.

codes.label: Declare a variable
codes.description: Declares a variable of the program. The declarations stand at the top of the program, one DEF per block.

codes.label: Indirect call
codes.description: Calls a program whose name stands in quotation marks or in a variable.

codes.label: Call with a path
codes.description: Calls a subprogram by its full path, with arguments: PCALL/path/NAME(…).

codes.label: Call from external storage
codes.description: Runs a program from a drive outside the control's program memory, such as a local, network or USB drive, named in quotation marks in brackets: EXTCALL("…").

codes.label: Section of a program
codes.description: CALL … BLOCK start TO end runs the part of a program between two labels.

codes.label: Siemens language mode
codes.description: The control reads the program in its own language again, after G291.

codes.label: ISO dialect mode
codes.description: From this block on the control reads the program in its ISO dialect, with Fanuc-style codes and words, until G290.

templates.label: Program start
templates.description: A description, the safe-start line for turning or milling, the units and the work offset.

params.label: Machining
params.help: The turning and the milling profile share this template; choose the line for your machine. Nothing is chosen until you pick one.

choices.label: Turning: G18, feed per revolution, X as a diameter
Milling: G17, feed per minute, no radius compensation

templates.label: Tool start
templates.description: Selects the tool by name with its cutting edge, starts constant cutting speed with the speed limit LIMS= and approaches with coolant.

params.label: Tool name
params.help: As in the tool list; no double quotes.

params.label: Highest spindle speed (rpm)
params.help: LIMS= limits the spindle speed under constant cutting speed.

templates.label: Stock removal (CYCLE95)
templates.description: Roughs and finishes along a contour that a subprogram or a labelled section describes, with the three feeds as arguments. Empty arguments keep the cycle's own setting.

params.label: Contour
params.help: The name of the contour subprogram, or the first and last label of the contour in this program.

params.label: Largest depth of cut (radius or diameter: verify)
params.help: Whether this is a radius or a diameter depends on DIAMON and on the cycle setting of the machine. Check it before the first run.

params.label: Finishing allowance along the contour
params.help: Instead of, or as well as, the allowances on Z and X.

choices.label: Roughing and finishing, along Z, outside (9)
Roughing and finishing, along Z, inside (11)

params.label: Lift-off from the contour
params.help: 0 lifts off by 1 mm.

templates.label: Thread turning (CYCLE99)
templates.description: Cuts a straight thread in several passes. The pitch is an argument, not the feed in force. Mode arguments the template does not ask for are written as 0 or empty (the cycle's own setting). The sample is an M20×1.5 outside thread.

params.label: Thread diameter at the end (X)
params.help: The same as at the start for a straight thread.

params.label: Infeed angle (°)
params.help: Positive feeds along the one flank, negative along the other, 0 straight in.

params.label: Machining
params.help: Decreasing cuts keep the chip area the same on every pass; all four feed in along one flank.

choices.label: Outside thread, rough and finish, decreasing cuts
Outside thread, rough and finish, equal cuts
Inside thread, rough and finish, decreasing cuts
Inside thread, rough and finish, equal cuts

templates.label: Tool end
templates.description: Back to the tool change position with coolant off and an optional stop.

templates.label: Tool change
templates.description: Loads the tool with M6, activates its cutting edge D, starts the spindle and approaches the start position.

params.label: Tool name
params.help: As in the tool list; no double quotes.

templates.label: Drilling (CYCLE81)
templates.description: Sets the drilling feed, makes CYCLE81 modal with MCALL, drills the first hole and ends the modal call. Add more positions before the closing MCALL; each one drills a hole.

params.label: Reference plane: top of the hole (Z)
Safety distance
params.help: Above the reference plane, without a sign.

params.label: Drilling feed (mm/min)
params.help: Written in its own block before MCALL. A feed written after MCALL would drill at once where the tool stands.

templates.label: Drilling with dwell (CYCLE82)
templates.description: Like CYCLE81 with a dwell at the bottom, for a counterbore or a flat bottom. The drilling feed is set before MCALL.

params.label: Reference plane: top of the hole (Z)
Safety distance
params.help: Above the reference plane, without a sign.

params.label: Drilling feed (mm/min)
params.help: Written in its own block before MCALL. A feed written after MCALL would drill at once where the tool stands.

params.label: Dwell at the bottom (s)
params.help: Seconds; the cycle reads a negative value as spindle revolutions.

templates.label: Deep-hole drilling (CYCLE83)
templates.description: Pecks to the final depth, breaking the chip or pulling out after each peck. The drilling feed is set before MCALL, which makes the cycle modal for the positions that follow.

params.label: Reference plane: top of the hole (Z)
Safety distance
params.help: Above the reference plane, without a sign.

params.label: Drilling feed (mm/min)
params.help: Written in its own block before MCALL. A feed written after MCALL would drill at once where the tool stands.

params.label: Depth of the first peck (Z, absolute)
Dwell at the start for chip removal (s)
Feed factor for the first peck

choices.label: Pull out to clear the chips (1)

templates.label: Rigid tapping (CYCLE84)
templates.description: Taps with the spindle under position control; the pitch and the speeds are arguments of the cycle, not the feed in force. MCALL makes it modal for the positions that follow.

params.label: Reference plane: top of the hole (Z)
Safety distance
params.help: Above the reference plane, without a sign.

params.label: Thread pitch (mm)
params.help: Positive for a right-hand thread, negative for a left-hand one.

params.label: Retract speed (rpm)
params.help: 0 retracts at the tapping speed.

templates.label: Program end
templates.description: Coolant and spindle off and the end of the program.
